svg.title: Four Checks Before Federal Filing
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-statutory-risk-decision-tree; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Checks Before Federal Filing; subtitle: Explicit stop, reroute, and proceed outcomes preserve fees and deadlines.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Evaluate the checks in sequence for each proposed dispute or batch. Statutory anchors include 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111, 45 CFR §§ 149.30 and 149.510, and HIPAA business-associate requirements in 45 CFR § 164.504(e). Verify current CMS operational guidance and applicable court orders when configuring deadline, fee, and batching rules.; caption: A missing fact is a work item, not permission to file. Every negative branch must identify the responsible person, next action, and remaining deadline.; stages: label: Authority and protected records; value: Complete → check two; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Yes: retain provider representation authority, required BAA terms, access controls, and relevant records. No: stop protected-data ingestion and filing until authority and handling arrangements are established; use de-identified samples for system testing.; label: Federal payment jurisdiction; value: Eligible → check three; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Yes: document covered service circumstances and why federal IDR applies. No: route to the applicable state process, contractual appeal, or other supported channel. Do not equate self-funded ERISA status with automatic eligibility or fully insured status with automatic exclusion.; label: Timing and batch validity; value: Valid → check four; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Yes: retain negotiation notices, business-day calculations, timely initiation evidence, and current batch criteria. No: remove incompatible claims or stop the filing. Apply the 90-calendar-day same-party, same-or-similar-item cooling-off restriction and its applicable post-period initiation window; never reset clocks through relabeling.; label: Evidence and collection economics; value: Positive → authorized filing; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Proceed only with a supportable offer and a positive risk-adjusted net collection estimate. Budget CMS administrative fees as non-refundable and losing or ineligible cases as unrecovered entity-fee exposure. Credit prevailing-party entity refunds only when confirmed; apply dismissal-specific rules rather than presuming a refund. Otherwise renegotiate, correct, or decline.

rect.title: label: Authority and protected records; value: Complete → check two; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Yes: retain provider representation authority, required BAA terms, access controls, and relevant records. No: stop protected-data ingestion and filing until authority and handling arrangements are established; use de-identified samples for system testing.

text.title: Yes: retain provider representation authority, required BAA terms, access controls, and relevant records. No: stop protected-data ingestion and filing until authority and handling arrangements are established; use de-identified samples for system testing.

No: route to the applicable state process, contractual appeal, or other supported channel. Do not equate self-funded ERISA status with automatic eligibility or fully insured status with automatic exclusion.

No: remove incompatible claims or stop the filing. Apply the 90-calendar-day same-party, same-or-similar-item cooling-off restriction and its applicable post-period initiation window; never reset clocks through relabeling.

Assumptions: Evaluate the checks in sequence for each proposed dispute or batch. Statutory anchors include 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111, 45 CFR §§ 149.30 and 149.510, and HIPAA business-associate requirements in 45 CFR § 164.504(e). Verify current CMS operational guidance and applicable court orders when configuring deadline, fee, and batching rules.
